**My pick for most iPhone 17 owners is the Anker Nano Power Bank (5K, MagGo, Slim).** If you want the thinnest and lightest one, get the Baseus Picogo Air. All of these are 5,000mAh, so they give a partial top-up rather than a full recharge.

| Pick | Thickness | Weight | Wireless | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseus Picogo Air AM71 | 0.27 in | 104 g | 7.5W | $69.99–$79.99, depending on color |
| Anker Nano 5K | 0.34 in | 122 g | 15W Qi2 | $54.99 |
| ReelCharge ReelSafe | 0.35 in | 119 g | 15W Qi2 | about $49.50 |

**Anker Nano Power Bank 5K: best all-around**
- It's Qi2-certified, charges at 15W, and Anker lists the iPhone 17 series as compatible. It's 0.34" thick and weighs 122 g.
- 9to5Mac says it's the closest alternative to Apple's own MagSafe battery. The reviewer has used it and says it feels premium and runs cooler than the competition.
- Anker says it charges at 20W over USB-C.
- Anker says cases thicker than 2.5 mm weaken the connection. Thick cases like OtterBox Defender won't work well.
- [Buy from Anker, $54.99](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank). [9to5Mac's review](https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/27/favorite-magsafe-iphone-battery-banks-right-now/) links an Amazon listing too.

**Baseus Picogo Air AM71: thinnest and lightest**
- Android Central's reviewer calls it the lightest, thinnest power bank she has used. It has no battery display, but you can tap it to your phone to check the charge in an app.
- The catch is wireless speed. Its 7.5W is the slowest here, and it costs the most. Wired output is 22.5W.
- [Buy on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GWPP9Q26). Android Central says it goes on sale often, so check the price first.

**ReelCharge ReelSafe: cheapest of the three slim Qi2 options**
- It has 15W Qi2 wireless, 20W wired, an LED display, and a semi-solid-state battery. Android Central tested it and rates it well. It's a lesser-known brand.
- The $49.50 listings are the ones tagged "LED | SSD." A third listing at $59.99 isn't tagged SSD, so check which version you're buying.
- [Buy on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0H34PD1WM)

**If you can accept a thicker one:** the INIU SnapGo Air is 10,000mAh with 25W Qi2.2 wireless and a built-in lanyard cable. It's 0.5" thick and weighs about 195 g, with 45W wired output. It's $42.99 on Amazon in black. The iPhone 17 supports Qi2.2, so it can use the 25W speed. [Buy on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0H448SDMB).

**Skip for now:** LISEN's P601 page is a wholesale listing with a 100-unit minimum, and its thickness and weight figures conflict. The 9to5Mac guide's cheapest Baseus pick ($24.99) is 7.5W only.

Prices are as of the review dates, so check them before buying.

 Another interesting fact: Apple’s [iPhone Air MagSafe battery](https://amzn.to/3SoRKO7) only supports up to 12W of charging, despite the iPhone Air supporting up to 20W of charging with MagSafe. The form factor is rather remarkable, and likely serves as the closest alternative to Apple’s MagSafe battery.
